summary_points: Document is electronically signed and filed in Document Management System.
Client is Arizona Solar One, project HEX replacement TES Solana.

Important instructions include removing orange-painted parts, checking plug tightness, notifying LOINTEK for warranty work, being cautious when entering the system, ensuring bolted joints remain tight, and reporting significant problems.
Table of contents includes sections on shipping/installation, start-up/operation, maintenance/reparations, and annexes with documentation and testing details.
Oil to Salt Heat Exchangers shipped with nitrogen gas for shipping.
Inspect for shipping damage immediately upon arrival.
Heaters should be stored on cribbing, not in contact with the ground.
Nitrogen blanketed heaters need regular inspection and pressure restoration.
Install each heater as shown on the General Arrangement Drawing.
Use nylon slings for lifting operations to avoid damaging equipment.
Do not confuse pulling lugs with lifting lugs during handling.
Proper rigging required for lifting Oil to Salt Heat Exchanger Systems
Fixed supports need shims for proper elevation
Anchor bolt stakeout must match equipment drill distribution
All bolt elements must be correctly installed before lifting
Pipelines should be blown before welding to equipment
Nitrogen protection is crucial for corrosion prevention
Any alterations or repairs must be made under LOINTEK direction
Oil to Salt Heat Exchanger System requires specific start-up, operation, and shut-down instructions.
Initial cold start-up involves heating up the system gradually and introducing salt carefully.
Warm start-up follows operational limits specified in another document.
Shut-down should prioritize stopping hot fluid flow before cold side.
Drainage procedures include protecting internals from corrosion and using nitrogen or inert gas.
Field welding must be qualified and witnessed by a Notified Body.
Shell removal requires careful support to prevent damage.
Bolted connections should have clean, defect-free joint surfaces.
Hydro test is required after all connections are welded.
Bolted connections should be tightened uniformly in a diametrically staggered pattern.
Torque values are based on studs well-lubricated with a heavy graphite and oil mixture.
Gasket selection should be in accordance with the original design.
Visual examination of tubesheet, tube ends, and inlet pass tube is recommended.
Penetrant test can detect damages in the weldings between the tube and the tubesheet.
Instructions cover plugging of Oil to Salt Heat Exchanger tubes in three categories: tube-end, safety, and tubesheet.
General preparation includes obtaining plugs from Lointek Procedure and cleaning the work area.
Welded plugs require specific precautions such as clean welding areas and avoiding free machining materials.
Tests for plugged tubes include bubble leak tests, penetrant examinations, and optional hydrostatic tests.
Pass partition cover plates can be removed using handles or nuts depending on access type.
Installation involves visual inspection, cleaning, and proper gasket handling to ensure equipment safety.
Hydrostatic test pressures must not be exceeded and verified on the nameplate.
Water temperature for hydrostatic testing should be at least 60°F (15.5°C).
